Subject: QBR infrastructure allocation and OKR check-in — capacity scenarios & unit economics

Team — kicking off the infra section for the July QBR. I want a compact, decision-ready pack that covers:
- 3 capacity scenarios (conservative / baseline / growth) with GPU counts, regional distribution, and burst vs reserved mixes
- Unit economics by model family (cost per 1k tokens served, cost per 1k embeddings, per-request overheads)
- Key levers: batching, KV / prefix caching, quantization profiles — estimated impact on spend and latency
- Ops runbooks / SLAs for warm pools and prewarmed KV caches (failure modes + fallback)

I've attached a simple template (qbr_requirement_template.xlsx) — please populate your sections and drop back by EOD 20-Jun. Concrete asks: current Q2 spend baseline, realized GPU utilization by pool, realistic uplift assumptions if we enable continuous batching and 2-tier caching for chat.

If you think we should loop procurement or an AWS rep early, flag it. I'll send a follow-up with a proposed slide skeleton.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR infrastructure allocation and OKR check-in — capacity scenarios & unit economics

Aisha — attaching a quick dump of the numbers I pulled together and a short runbook. High level summary up top, details below. Attachment: gpu_runbook_v2.pdf

Summary bullets: 
- Current quarterly GPU spend (Q2 run-rate): ~$1.23M (all-hosted + dedicated blends)
- Observed average utilization across production pools: 62% (stdev 9%)
- Batching gains (continuous batching spop): expected +9–14% throughput per GPU for chat-heavy workloads; latency tail increases ~15–25ms median if we accept 50–100ms batching windows
- KV/prefix caching (APIs with heavy prompt reuse): measured 18% fewer tokens served in pilot (superchat workload) — roughly 16% CPU/GPU token cost reduction once cache hits are served from local RAM
- Practical reserve vs burst: mixing 60% reserved / 40% burst gives good latency predictability and ~12% cost uplift vs fully reserved but with better availability during spikes

Operational notes (short): warm pool sizing should target 30–40% of peak concurrent sessions for low-latency chat; prewarmed KV cache eviction TTLs tuned by workload (recommend 15–60 mins depending on session churn).

I'll push my sheet to the drive link and tag the model families; Marcus

Thanks Marcus and Aisha — useful start. A couple of strategic thoughts for the QBR pack: 
- Please split unit economics by model class (small-gen, base-gen, instruction tuned, embedding-only). For each, show cost per 1k tokens at current quantization profile + projected cost if we adopt 4-bit quantization for that family.
- Two scenario asks: Conservative (5% growth, maintain 62% util) and Aggressive (30% growth, increase util to 75% via batching/caching). For the Aggressive case, add a sensitivity table: if batching increases tail latency by >40ms, what's the user-facing error/abandon rate assumption?
- Include a short slide on risks: degradation of latency SLAs, cache warmup fragility, and cross-region data-egress cost if we shift more traffic to APAC.

I'm attaching a quick forecast template I used (scenario_model_20270623.csv). Will drop a couple of runway figures for finance to review.

Rishi
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Team — good thread. Two operational/OKR asks before the pack is final: 
1) Align on measurable OKRs we can defend at the exec QBR: 
   - Throughput/$ (tokens per $1k) target for next quarter
   - % of interactive traffic served from local cache (target 20% -> 30%)
   - P95 latency budget for chat (current 380ms) — propose we declare 420ms soft for Aggressive scenario with compensating rollout plan
2) I want a single slide that clearly maps which engineering / infra owners will be on call if we push Aggressive: who owns prewarm, batch windows, fallback to smaller model, and cross-region routing.

Let's review live — I propose a 30-min sync on Wed 30-Jun at 4:00pm PT (calendar invite attached). Agenda: review two scenarios, confirm OKRs, decide reserve/burst split. Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.internal/infra-qbr-20270630

Vivek
SVP, Platform
